problems.title: Compare powers with base three
problems.question: Solve $3^{\sqrt x}<3^{x-2}$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Base 3 is increasing, so $\sqrt x<x-2$.
steps: This requires x>2. Squaring gives x<(x−2)², or (x−1)(x−4)>0. With x>2, the answer is x>4.

problems.title: Volume of a regular hexagonal pyramid
problems.question: Base side is 2 and lateral edge is 3. Find the volume.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: The circumradius is 2, so $h=\sqrt{9-4}=\sqrt5$. Base are a $S=6\cdot(\sqrt3/4)2^2=6\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Unknown logarithm bases
problems.question: Solve $\log_{3x}4=\log_{2x}8$. Write the root a/b in lowest terms and find a+b.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
steps: The bases must be positive and unequal to 1. Cross multiplication gives 2ln(2x)=3ln(3x), so 4x²=27x³ and x=4/27. Both bases are valid.

problems.title: Reciprocal exponential bases
problems.question: Solve $(\sqrt5-2)^{x-2}>(\sqrt5+2)^{1-2x}$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
steps: Rewrite the left side with base √5+2>1 and exponent 2−x. Require 2−x>1−2x, or x>−1.

problems.title: Equal lateral edges above a parallelogram
problems.question: A pyramid has a parallelogram base, lateral edges 8, base diagonal 12 and base side 8. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Equal lateral edges put all base vertices on a circle. A cyclic parallelogram is a rectangle.
steps: Its circumradius is 6, so h=√(64−36)=2√7. The other rectangle side is √(144−64)=4√5, giving are a 32√5. Divide Sh by 3.

problems.title: Distance from a cylinder axis
problems.question: Cylinder height is 1/π, volume 9. A vertical section has one third the axial-section are a. Find its distance from the axis.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: $\pi r^2h=9$ gives $r=3$. The section chord has length $2r/3=2$.
steps: Half the chord is 1, so its distance is √(3²−1²).

problems.title: Range of a logarithmic expression
problems.question: Find the range of $12/[1+\lg(100+x^2)]-2$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
steps: The denominator ranges over [3,∞), so the fraction ranges over (0,4]. Subtract 2.

problems.title: A twelfth logarithmic progression term
problems.question: $\lg(a^3b^7),\lg(a^5b^{12}),\lg(a^8b^{15})$ begin a nonconstant arithmetic progression. Term 12 is $\lg(b^n)$. Find n.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Put $A=\lg a, B=\lg b$. The progression condition gives $2(5A+12B)=3A+7B+8A+15B$, hence $A=2B$.
steps: The first term is 13B and the common difference is 9B. Term 12 is 13B+11·9B=112B. Nonconstancy gives B≠0, so n=112.

problems.title: Quadrants of a logarithmic region
problems.question: In which quadrants can $\log_{0.199}(x^2+y^2)<-1$ hold?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Because the base is less than 1, $x^2+y^2>1/0.199$.
steps: This is the exterior of a circle centred at the origin. It contains points in every quadrant.

problems.title: Area determined by logarithm domains
problems.question: Find the region are a satisfying $|\log_3(y-x)|+1>0$, $|\log_3(10-x-y)|+2>0$, and $(\log_{0.3}x)^2\ge0$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Where defined, all three inequalities hold automatically. The domains require $x>0, y>x, x+y<10$.
steps: These bound a triangle with vertices (0,0),(0,10),(5,5). Its are a is 10·5/2. Open boundaries do not change are a.

problems.title: A sphere inside a cone frustum
problems.question: A frustum has an inscribed sphere, and its volume is twice the sphere volume. Find the large-to-small base-radius ratio.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: For base radii R, r, tangency in the axial trapezoid gives $h=2\sqrt{Rr}$ and sphere radius $\rho=\sqrt{Rr}$.
steps: The volume ratio is (R²+Rr+r²)/(2Rr)=2. Put t=R/r>1: t²−3t+1=0. Choose the root greater than 1.

problems.title: Cone volume from a quarter-arc section
problems.question: A plane through a cone apex makes 45° with the base and cuts off a quarter-circle arc. Height is 6. Find volume.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: The chord distance from the base centre is $r/\sqrt2$. Thus $6/(r/\sqrt2)=1$.

problems.title: A prescribed solution of an inequality
problems.question: Which listed k makes x=1 a solution of $4^x-k2^x\le0$?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: At x=1, $4-2k\le0$, so $k\ge2$.
steps: Only the listed number 2.1 meets the bound.

problems.title: Order three powers
problems.question: Order $A=(\sqrt{17}-4)^{5-\sqrt{23}}$, $B=(\sqrt{17}-4)^{5-\sqrt{21}}$, $C=(\sqrt{11}-3)^{4-3\sqrt2}$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Both bases lie between 0 and 1. Also $0<5-\sqrt{23}<5-\sqrt{21}$, while $4-3\sqrt2<0$.
steps: The decreasing first-base power gives B<A<1. The negative exponent makes C>1.

problems.title: Four nested logarithms
problems.question: Find the length of the domain interval of $\log_{0.5}(\log_4(\log_{1/4}(\log_{16}x)))$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: The outer log requires $\log_4(\log_{1/4}(\log_{16}x))>0$.
steps: This means log₁/₄(log₁₆x)>1, or 0<log₁₆x<1/4. Hence 1<x<16^(1/4)=2.

problems.title: Concentric insphere and circumsphere
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has inscribed and circumscribed spheres with the same centre. Which listed ratio of their radii is possible?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Write base half-side b, height h, inradius r, circumradius R. Then $h=R+r$, $R^2=r^2+2b^2$, and $r=(h-r)b/\sqrt{h^2+b^2}$.
steps: Put t=r/h. The second relation gives b²/h²=(1−2t)/2. The tangency relation gives b²/h²=t²/(1−2t). Thus 1−2t=√2t, so h/r=2+√2. Therefore R/r=1+√2 and r/R=√2−1.
problems.note: The wording does not order the two radii. The reverse ratio is 1+√2, which is not among the choices.

problems.title: A sum of cubes from two symmetric sums
problems.question: If lg(x+y)=z and lg(x²+y²)=z+1, write $x^3+y^3=a10^{3z}+b10^{2z}$ and find a+b.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
steps: Use x³+y³=s³−3xys=−s³/2+15s². Thus a=−1/2, b=15.

problems.title: Integer roots of a log inequality
problems.question: How many integers satisfy lg(x−40)+lg(60−x)<2?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Domain $40<x<60$. The inequality becomes $(x-40)(60-x)<100$, or $100-(x-50)^2<100$.
steps: All 19 integers 41 through 59 work except 50.

problems.title: Can this equation have four roots?
problems.question: For which a does $(\log_7x)^2+|\log_7x|=a$ have four distinct roots?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: Put $u=|\log_7x|\ge0$. The function $u^2+u$ is strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$.
steps: There is at most one u. A positive u gives only two x values, 7ᵘ and 7⁻ᵘ; u=0 gives one. Four are impossible.

problems.title: Box circumsphere
problems.question: A rectangular box has total edge length 112 and surface are a 384. Find the circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
steps: The space diagonal satisfies d²=(a+b+c)²−2(ab+bc+ca)=784−384=400. The radius is half the diagonal.

problems.title: An integer logarithm condition
problems.question: Integers a≥2, b≥1, c≥0 satisfy logₐb=c and a+b+c=2025. Which listed value can 2a+b+c take?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: The target is $2025+a$. Also $b=a^c$.
steps: Take c=1 and b=a. Then 2a+1=2025 gives a=b=1012. The target is 2025+1012=3037, one of the choices.

problems.title: Volume from perpendicular lateral edges
problems.question: Three lateral edges from one tetrahedron vertex have length 3. Their pairwise angles are 90°,90°,60°. Find volume.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: One edge is perpendicular to the plane of the other two. The base triangle has are a $3\cdot3\sin60^\circ/2$.
steps: Its are a is 9√3/4 and the height is 3. V=Sh/3.

problems.title: Distinct integer exponents
problems.question: How many quadruples of pairwise distinct integers x, y, z, t satisfy $x\lg2+y\lg3+z\lg5+t\lg7=2024$?
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
steps: Uniqueness of prime exponents, also for rational products with negative exponents, forces x=z=2024 and y=t=0. These are not pairwise distinct.

problems.title: Finite numbers of integer solutions
problems.question: Which have finitely many integer solutions? I: $\sqrt{x^2-3x-2}>2x-1$; II: $\log_{0.2}(x-4)>-4$; III: $3^{x^2-4x-100}<7$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: I holds for every sufficiently negative integer, so it has infinitely many. II gives $0<x-4<625$.
steps: II lies in a bounded interval. III gives x²−4x−100<log₃7; a positive-leading quadratic is below a constant only on a bounded interval. Both therefore contain finitely many integers.

problems.title: Tetrahedron circumradius and logarithms
problems.question: A regular tetrahedron has edge log₁₉₉a and circumradius log₁₉₉b. Find $(\log_ab)^2$.
problems.idea: Keep the domain while simplifying the equation or geometry.
formulas: For edge l, $R=l\sqrt6/4$. Also $\log_ab=\log_{199}b/\log_{199}a=R/l$.
steps: Square √6/4.
